html:
The Araona are a small Indigenous people of the Amazon lowlands of northern Bolivia, living on the upper Manupari River in La Paz department. They speak a language of the Tacanan family, and most of them still use it every day.

The rubber boom of the late 1800s nearly wiped them out: rubber and Brazil nut collectors raided the region, and disease spread. Only a few dozen survived. Since the 1960s their numbers have slowly grown, and today there are around a hundred Araona, on their own Indigenous territory. Their neighbours include other Tacanan peoples and the wider Amazon peoples.
